hook.description: Cold open, no establishing shot: a stop-motion elderly-styled couple (long-nosed woman reading a book, bald man in glasses on his phone) sit up in bed under a lamp. Wife opens with a flat accusation, 'You snore.'
hook.why_it_works: Drops the viewer straight into the middle of a marital spat with zero context, so the blunt, deadpan delivery and the visual gag of two tired, expressionless puppet faces creates instant intrigue about what happens next in under 2 seconds.

setup.description: Husband reflexively denies it ('No, I don't.'), and the wife immediately one-ups the denial with a flat reveal, 'I recorded it,' establishing that she has proof and raising the stakes of the argument.

conflict.description: Husband demands 'Delete it.' and the wife flatly refuses with 'I can't.' A brief held silence follows as his stunned/confused expression (visible in the periodic keyframes) lets the refusal land before the reveal, building tension over why she can't (or won't) delete the recording.

punchline.description: The wife reveals the twist in two beats: 'I play it when you travel' (she deliberately keeps and replays his snoring while he's away) followed by a topper, 'It helps me sleep' -- subverting the expectation that the recording was blackmail leverage and instead revealing an oddly affectionate, absurd habit.

ending.description: No further dialogue; the scene holds on the couple's reactions (husband's crooked smile, wife's tired stare) for a beat before the frame is overlaid, then replaced by a black title card.
ending.cta_or_text_overlay: Yellow serif title 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE', white subtitle 'CREATED BY NIN.', and a yellow ribbon graphic reading 'NEW EPISODE DAILY'; an 'Episode 36' label is also burned into the top-left corner of the live-action frame earlier in the video.

beat_map.description: Wife's blunt opening accusation 'You snore.' with no preamble, over static two-shot of the couple in bed.
Husband denies it ('No, I don't.'); wife reveals she recorded him ('I recorded it.'), establishing the evidence at stake.
Husband demands 'Delete it.', wife refuses 'I can't.', followed by a short silent reaction beat that holds the tension before the explanation.
Two-part reveal: 'I play it when you travel.' then the topper 'It helps me sleep.', subverting expectations of blackmail into an absurd comfort habit.
Silent reaction hold on both characters' faces, then dissolve to the 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / Created by Nin. / New Episode Daily' branded title card.

narrative_notes: This 14.4s reel is shorter than a typical 20-25s reel and compresses the arc into a single static bedroom two-shot with no scene/location change (scene_boundaries.json shows only one real content scene, 0-13.1s, followed by a 1.2s pure title-card scene). There is no traditional 'setup' establishing normalcy before conflict -- the video opens already inside the conflict (hook and setup are fused into the accusation-and-denial exchange). The punchline itself is two-beat (reveal + topper 'It helps me sleep'), which is common in this format to land a second, bigger laugh right before the ending. The ending carries no spoken CTA; the 'CTA' is purely the visual brand card (title, creator credit, 'New Episode Daily' ribbon) fading in over the frozen final expressions, functioning as a series-recognition/follow hook rather than a narrative resolution.
